not_measured: Whether `claude --resume <id>` reuses the id it is given. The runtime assumes it does and lifts an ended mark on any session_started, which is safe either way: a new id is a new row, and a reused id is correctly reopened.
Any harness other than Claude Code, and any platform other than macOS.
question: does /clear retire the session id, or reuse it?
what_it_settles: A SessionEnd names an id that is genuinely finished, whatever its reason. The turn after a /clear belongs to a different id, so the cleared one never takes another prompt. An earlier reading of the a7 arm concluded the opposite, that /clear proves a SessionEnd does not mean an ending; that conclusion was drawn without the ids and is corrected here. What a7 shows is that the PROCESS survives, which is a different claim from the session id surviving.
why_the_ids_are_not_recorded: The finding is that the two ids differ, which the boolean carries. A real session prefix is the class of value DRC-4382 leaked past a masker whose own docstring named the hazard, and it would add nothing here.

notes: reason_separates_clean_from_killed is null, not false: see the note record. A SessionEnd always names a session id that is finished; what a /clear shows is that the PROCESS can continue, under a NEW id. The a8 arm measured that and corrects an earlier reading of a7 which, having no ids, concluded a SessionEnd may not be an ending at all.

arrangement: Claude Code 2.1.261 on macOS, eight arms, each its own session and its own capture directory. Hooks were installed project-locally in a scratch directory, never in the operator's settings, so nothing here could fire for another session. Interactive arms ran under tmux 3.7c on a socket this recorder mints, and the first-run trust prompt was answered as part of starting the session rather than measured.
not_measured: Any harness other than Claude Code.
Power loss, an OOM kill, and a system shutdown, none of which were run. A SIGKILL is the nearest measured proxy for the first two.
Logout, which is the one documented-sounding ending still undriven; the reason vocabulary is closed but these three values are not proven to exhaust it.
turn_open_at_end_caveat: Three terminal-closed arms were driven with a prompt in flight and only a5c had the turn still open at the kill; a5 and a5b had a Stop arrive first, which their own records show. a2 and a3 were both genuinely mid-turn, so the mid-turn case is covered for the signal question by the signal arms rather than by the terminal arms.
why_every_arm_records_session_started_ob: The first run of the interactive arms parked on that trust prompt, so the session never started and the recorder saw no events at all. Read without the gate that is indistinguishable from a silent death, and would have produced exactly the wrong verdict. An arm proves nothing unless a SessionStart was observed for it.
why_reason_separates_clean_from_killed_i: Because it is neither true nor false as asked. `prompt_input_exit` is distinctive and means a deliberate quit inside the session. `other` is not: it covers a headless run that completed normally AND a SIGTERM AND a closed terminal. So the field separates one deliberate ending from everything else, and does not separate a clean ending from a killed one. A boolean here would assert more than the arms support.
why_the_a7_reading_was_corrected: a7 established that the process survives a /clear, and was read as showing that a SessionEnd need not mean an ending. It carried no session ids, so it could not separate the process surviving from the id surviving. a8 measured the ids: they differ, so the id does end and only the process continues. The stronger reading was drawn from evidence that could not support it, which is the failure this file's own gate exists to catch.
why_the_clear_arm_was_added_after_the_ot: A comment in events.py says Claude fires SessionEnd on /clear as well as on exit, which if true breaks any consumer that reads a SessionEnd as an ending. It was written from prior knowledge and had never been measured. It is correct, and the arm adds the fact the comment does not carry: the reason is `clear`, distinct from every other ending, and a SessionStart follows within 0.3s while the process keeps working.
